note_tweet.text:
The United States of America crossed a major demographic threshold more than a decade ago, when babies from racial and ethnic minority groups collectively became the majority of the country’s youngest population.

The U.S. Census Bureau reported in May 2012 that 50.4% of Americans under the age of one were minorities as of July 1, 2011, compared with 49.5% in the 2010 Census. For that calculation, “minority” meant anyone who was not non-Hispanic, single-race White.

The demographic shift remains visible in the latest birth data. The U.S. recorded 3,628,934 births in 2024, of which 1,783,156 were to non-Hispanic White mothers, about 49.1%.

Births to mothers in all other reported racial and ethnic categories combined therefore exceeded those to non-Hispanic White mothers.
